voyage.name: Go San Diego Card
voyage.content: Covers admission and express entry to over 40 attractions, including Sea World San Diego, Legoland California, San Diego Zoo, San Diego Zoo Safari Park, USS Midway Museum, Birch Aquarium, and all Balboa Park museums.

voyage.name: Southern California CityPass
voyage.content: Gives you one day each at SeaWorld San Diego, Legoland California, and a 3-day park hopper ticket for Disneyland, as well as one-day admission to either the San Diego Zoo or the San Diego Zoo Safari Park for an additional fee if purchased online.

voyage.name: Gaslamp Quarter
voyage.content: Home to a number of historic Victorian-era buildings, such as the Louis Bank of Commerce, the Backesto Building, the Old City Hall, the Yuma Building, and a whole bunch of other beautiful old structures.

voyage.name: Gaslamp Museum at the Davis Horton House
voyage.price: Museum $5/adult, children free; $8 combo ticket with San Diego Chinese History Museum; Walking tours $20/adult, $15/senior/military, $10/student, children free
voyage.content: Previously called the William Heath Davis House, this museum is the headquarters of the Gaslamp Quarter Historical Foundation. The visitor center here offers information for self-guided tours of the district as well as a guided walking tour of the district that leaves every Saturday at 11AM, and Thursday at 1PM. Hosts a festival every St. Patrick's Day.

voyage.name: Maritime Museum of San Diego
voyage.price: $16 adults, $13 seniors/military/students, $8 children, free for children under 4 (packages which include sailing excursions are available)
voyage.content: Home to a number of historic sea vessels, including the Star of India, the world's oldest active sailing ship, the Berkeley, an 1898 steam ferryboat, the Californian, a replica sailing ship, the Medea, a 1904 steam yacht, the HMS Surprise, another replica sailing ship, and a B-39 Soviet Attack Submarine.

voyage.name: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego
voyage.price: $10 adults, $5 seniors/students, military/25 and under free (free admission the third Thursday of the month)
voyage.content: Just north of Santa Fe Depot, this museum holds a part of the museum's collection over 4,000 works.

voyage.name: San Diego Chinese Historical Museum
voyage.price: $5/adult, children free, $8 combo ticket with Gaslamp Museum
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to Chinese history, culture and art. Includes exhibits on the Chinese experience in America.

voyage.name: San Diego Firehouse Museum
voyage.content: Dedicated to the history of firefighting in San Diego.

voyage.name: USS Midway Aircraft Carrier Museum
voyage.price: $34 adults, $34 seniors, $34 students, $24 retired military/youth, children under 5 and active military free (discount if purchased online)
voyage.content: Take a self-guided tour of the USS Midway (CV-41), a former aircraft carrier of the US Navy. The Midway is home to a collection of former naval aircraft housed on her expansive flight deck. Guided tours and displays offer a unique look into the life aboard and of a powerful old warhorse.

voyage.name: San Diego Civic Theatre
voyage.content: Popular shows and musicals with some amazing performances.

voyage.name: San Diego Padres
voyage.price: Tickets $15-$120, depending on section and date of game; ballpark tours $12 adults, $10 military, $9 seniors, $8 children
voyage.content: See the Major League Baseball Padres play at Petco Park. The stadium, modeled after other "retro" ballparks, has many unique elements, such as the Western Metal Supply Co. building, a historic warehouse which is incorporated into the left-field seats. Price range for tickets varies widely, from $15-20 for a spot on the grassy lawn beyond the outfield wall (the "Park at the Park") to over $50 for a seat behind home pl

voyage.name: San Diego Symphony
voyage.content: Somewhat in the shadow of the mighty Los Angeles Philharmonic, but still a top notch symphony orchestra. See website for the current season.

voyage.name: Amici Park
voyage.address: at corner of Date and State Streets
voyage.content: A small park in Little Italy, notable for its bocce (a popular sport in Italy) courts. You can also find Italian recipes engraved onto the sidewalk plaques and tables around the park.

voyage.name: Children's Park
voyage.address: south of Island Avenue between Front St. and First Avenue
voyage.content: An unusual park with lots of grassy hills, shade trees, and a large water feature. Unfortunately, this park is usually occupied by homeless, so it wouldn't be a safe destination for children.

voyage.name: Embarcadero Park
voyage.address: south of Seaport Village behind the convention center
voyage.content: Also known as the Marina Park, Embarcadero Park is split into two parts, north and south, which shelter the marina. Very pleasant, with lots of trees, grass, and good views of the harbor. You can access the north park by walking through the Seaport Village shopping center, and you can reach the south park by going around the back side of the convention center.

voyage.name: Gaslamp Quarter Park
voyage.address: at Fifth Avenue and L Street
voyage.content: A small square next to the Gaslamp Quarter trolley station with a small water fountain. Good views of the convention center.

voyage.name: Horton Plaza Park
voyage.address: south of Broadway between Fourth and Third Avenue
voyage.content: A historic square just north of the shopping center of the same name. A large fountain marks the center of the park.

voyage.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Promenade
voyage.address: along the north side of Harbor Drive between First Avenue and Fifth Avenue
voyage.content: A linear park honoring the late civil rights activist.

voyage.name: Pantoja Park
voyage.content: A small park surrounded by a residential area.

voyage.name: Park at the Park
voyage.address: south of J Street between Seventh and Tenth Avenue
voyage.content: For the 81 Padres home game days, this grassy berm overlooking Petco Park is closed to the general public, open as a place to view the game for the price of a ticket. But for the other 284 days of the year, the park is open to the public. The park has a small baseball diamond, a playground, and there are various monuments to the achievements of the Padres, such as a statue of star player Tony Gwynn nearby.

voyage.name: San Diego Comic-Con International
voyage.content: For four days every July, one of the world's largest fan conventions descends on Downtown San Diego, flooding the convention center with over 100,000 attendees. Since its comic book origins, the convention has expanded into virtually every genre of pop culture, drawing Hollywood celebrities, major television producers, toy manufacturers, video game designers, and top-name anime and manga creators, offering sneak peek

voyage.name: Seaport Village
voyage.content: A shopping and dining complex overlooking the bay, with a recreated historic "seaside village" look. Nearly 70 shops and restaurants and an antique carousel.

voyage.name: Seaport Fudge Factory
voyage.content: Gorgeous shop with very well priced and excellent chocolates. All candies are made fresh daily on premises.

voyage.name: Basic
voyage.content: Outstanding thin crust pizza in a renovated warehouse space. Open late. Features both red (with tomato sauce) and white (cheese only) pies.

voyage.name: Bencotto Italian Kitchen
voyage.content: Modern and classic hand-made pasta dishes. Multi-year winner of critics and readers choice for Best Italian in San Diego Magazine.

voyage.name: Kansas City Barbeque
voyage.content: Unpretentious barbeque on paper plates. Unique interior with friendly staff and customers. Bar on premises.

voyage.name: Knotty Barrel
voyage.content: Cool gastropub with a great menu and wonderful selection of draft beers. Try a sample of four beers for $7 to see what you like. If none of the draft beers suit your taste, there's a multitude of other beers from all over the world listed on the chalkboard.

voyage.name: The Mission
voyage.content: Third and newest of the popular locally owned breakfast restaurant. Avoid the lines at the North Park and Mission Beach locations by coming here. Vegetarian offerings for the diet conscious. Only open for breakfast and lunch from 8AM - 3PM.

voyage.name: Mona Lisa Restaurant & Deli
voyage.content: Enjoy Sicilian style favorites and some of the best pizza in town at this family-oriented restaurant. Deli has large selection of Italian imports and is a great place to grab a sandwich.

voyage.name: Underbelly
voyage.content: Serves tonkotsu (pork broth) and vegetarian ramen. Gets crowded, expect to wait for seating if you arrive during the lunch or dinner rush. There is also a North Park location with a slightly different menu.

voyage.name: Brian's 24
voyage.content: As its name suggests, it's open 24/7. Tasty but fairly standard American food.

voyage.name: Neighborhood
voyage.content: Extremely popular small gastropub. Good burgers and sandwiches. Interesting beer selection.

voyage.name: Hodad's
voyage.content: Local favorite with great burgers, milkshakes, and not a lot else. Lively little spot with funky decor. There is also a location in Ocean Beach.

voyage.name: Fifth Avenue
voyage.content: This section of Fifth Ave contains many of the most popular clubs and bars in San Diego, and is typically seen as the heart of San Diego’s nightlife.

voyage.name: Princess Pub
voyage.content: Traditional British pub.

voyage.name: Sogno Divino
voyage.content: Wine bar and appetizers, relaxing environment.

voyage.name: Waterfront
voyage.content: One of San Diego's oldest drinking establishments and best dive bars.

voyage.name: El Dorado
voyage.content: Western-themed hipster hangout with good cocktails, rotating DJs, and a fun dance floor. A world away from the usual bottleservice & bouncers experience at many downtown SD clubs.

voyage.name: Bootlegger
voyage.content: Popular sports bar with good bar food and DJs at night.

voyage.name: Ballast Point
voyage.content: Little Italy tasting room and gastropub for one of San Diego's best known craft brewers. Several other locations around the city.

voyage.name: The Field
voyage.content: Irish pub literally shipped over piece by piece from Ireland and reassembled. Good food and drinks, and frequent live Irish music.

voyage.name: Hostel on 3rd
voyage.content: Hostel with easy access to the historic Gaslamp District. They have 2 bed private rooms, 4 bed mixed, 4 bed female and 6 bed mixed dorms. Most of them with a sink and a closet. Amenities include free wifi, free luggage storage, and free breakfast.

voyage.name: Hostelling International San Diego-Downtown
voyage.price: Rates start at around $25 for dorm rooms and around $65 for private rooms (rates vary)
voyage.content: It's in Gaslamp Quarter, clean, friendly, and offers 24-hour desk service, free breakfast, laundry facilities, lockers, and Wi-Fi. This hostel is part of a non-profit organization, HI-USA. The only hostel in this area to offer air conditioned rooms with iPod dock alarm clocks. Also offers free activities including: Walking tours, pub crawls, a screen printing workshop and bicycle tours. In addition there are three do

voyage.name: ITH Adventure Hostel
voyage.content: A friendly and cozy hostel that offers free breakfast and free dinner daily. Also they provide free adventure activities that guests can go on to enjoy San Diego.

voyage.name: Lucky D's Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm beds start around $20/night, privates around $50-60/person
voyage.content: Fun hostel in San Diego's trendy East Village. The hostel offers free breakfast, free dinners, free internet, free house phone, free pub crawl and free use of linens and towels. They also run a weekly tour to Tijuana.

voyage.name: La Pensione Hotel
voyage.content: In Little Italy, this lovely hotel has 75 small rooms with views of the bustling neighborhood. Parking is quite tight here, but the place is quite affordable at around $80/night.

voyage.name: USA Hostels San Diego
voyage.price: Dorm beds start around $20/night, privates around $50-60/person
voyage.content: Small hostel in the Gaslamp Quarter. The hostel offers free breakfasts, wireless access, lockers, a laundry room, and bike rentals. They run a tour to Tijuana on Saturdays.

voyage.name: Bristol Hotel
voyage.content: A contemporary and casual hotel, the Bristol features an unusually large pop art collection.

voyage.name: Comfort Inn Gaslamp Convention Center
voyage.content: A 100% non-smoking hotel in the Gaslamp Quarter.

voyage.name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Downtown
voyage.content: A unique 245-room hotel where timeless charm is blended seamlessly with sophisticated comfort of modern guest accommodations. Ideal location in the Gaslamp Quarter.

voyage.name: Gaslamp Plaza Suites
voyage.content: Housed in a beautiful historic building, this hotel offers lovely rooms and complimentary breakfast - served on the rooftop terrace (weather permitting).

voyage.name: Horton Grand Hotel
voyage.content: A luxurious Victorian-era hotel in the Gaslamp Quarter.

voyage.name: Marriott Gaslamp Quarter
voyage.content: 22-floor hotel in the Gaslamp neighborhood with most of the services and features typical of Marriotts (sadly, no pool or jacuzzi). Rooftop bar, on-site restaurant.

voyage.name: Doubletree San Diego Downtown
voyage.content: Complimentary airport shuttle, extensive amenities and friendly staff.

voyage.name: Alma San Diego Downtown
voyage.content: Rates start at $169 a night.

voyage.name: Manchester Grand Hyatt
voyage.content: This hotel has over 1600 rooms, making it the largest hotel in San Diego. It's next to the Convention Center, and consists of two towers that are connected on the bottom four floors.

voyage.name: Omni Hotel
voyage.content: A modern luxury hotel connected to Petco Park via a skybridge across the street, the Omni was built along the new ballpark and has a few baseball relics inside, such as Joe DiMaggio's cleats in the lobby, Babe Ruth's 1932 contract with the Yankees in the Presidential Suite, and a broken bat autographed by Willie Mays in the fifth-floor hallway.

voyage.name: U.S. Grant Hotel
voyage.content: A luxurious and historic hotel across the street from the Horton Plaza Square. It was built by Ulysses S. Grant's son, who later became a real estate developer in San Diego.

voyage.name: Mission San Diego de Alcalá
voyage.content: The first of the Spanish California missions, founded in 1769 by Junipero Serra for the purposes of converting the native peoples who lived in the area at the time. In its long history, the mission has been the site of the first Christian burial and the first execution in California, saw bloodshed between the Spanish settlers and native peoples, and served as an armory in the years following U.S. annexation of Califo

voyage.name: Heritage Park
voyage.content: A park in Old Town ringed with historic Victorian houses.

voyage.name: Immaculate Conception Church
voyage.content: A historic Mission-style church in Old Town dating back to 1919.

voyage.name: Mormon Battalion Visitors' Center of San Diego
voyage.content: A monument to the hundreds of Mormons who fought in the US-Mexican War.

voyage.name: Presidio Park
voyage.content: Perched on the hill above Old Town, this large park is the site of the old presidio (fort) that once protected the Spanish settlement of San Diego. The park contains canyons, tall trees, flowering plants, and grassy hillsides as well as several memorials and historic landmarks, including the Junipero Serra Museum (see below) and the partially excavated presidio. The grassy lawns and hilltop views make it a great plac

voyage.name: Junipero Serra Museum
voyage.content: Take the time to visit the historic site of what used to be the first ever California Mission, located in Presidio Park on the hill above Old Town. The museum includes exhibits on the life of Old Town and a tower which offers magnificent views of the area.

voyage.name: Sheriff's Museum
voyage.content: Learn the history of the San Diego Sheriff's Department.

voyage.name: Whaley House
voyage.price: Daytime admission $13.30 adults, $9.50 seniors/children, free for children 5 and under. Nighttime admission more
voyage.content: The oldest brick building and most famous haunted house in San Diego. Built in 1856, the north room of the museum served as the County Courthouse in 1869. The structure includes period furnishings and other antique displays. Come during the Halloween season for special night tours.

voyage.name: Robinson-Rose House Visitor Center
voyage.content: To begin touring, the best place to start is the visitor’s center, which includes a model of what the area looked like in 1872, maps, information about touring, and information about the area’s history. Free guided walking tours of Old Town depart daily at 11AM and 2PM.

voyage.name: Altamirano-Pedrorena House
voyage.content: Built in 1869, as a family residence, but is now the site of a rock, gem, and jewelry shop.

voyage.name: Black Hawk Smithy & Stable
voyage.content: Established in 1860. At the site, visitors can watch blacksmithing and other demonstrations.

voyage.name: Casa de Estudillo
voyage.content: A beautiful historic adobe house that has been lovingly restored to its original appearance.

voyage.name: Light-Freeman House
voyage.content: Built in 1830, the house was an adobe saloon and provision stores until it became the American Hotel around 1856.

voyage.name: Mason Street Schoolhouse
voyage.content: Established around 1865, this was the first public school house in San Diego. The school offers daily tours, and visitors can sit at the desk and examine the books on display.

voyage.name: San Diego Courthouse
voyage.content: The original courthouse, which dates back to 1847.

voyage.name: San Diego Union Museum
voyage.content: The first office of the San Diego Union newspaper.

voyage.name: Seeley Stable Museum
voyage.content: A reconstructed stage coach stop with a collection of vintage carriages inside.

voyage.name: Snapdragon Stadium
voyage.content: Opened in September 2022 on the former site of San Diego Stadium as the new home of the San Diego State Aztecs college football team. The women's soccer team San Diego Wave FC (see below) and men's rugby team San Diego Legion (also below) also play here, and the city's team in Major League Soccer, San Diego FC, will start play here in 2025.

voyage.name: San Diego Toreros
voyage.content: NCAA Division I teams representing the University of San Diego. The basketball team plays their home games at the Jenny Craig Pavilion on the USD campus. The Toreros college baseball team plays at Cunningham Stadium and their college football team plays at Torero Stadium (both also on the USD campus). USD competes in the West Coast Conference in most sports; since the WCC doesn't sponsor football, the Toreros play th

voyage.name: San Diego Wave FC
voyage.content: Started play in 2022 in the National Women's Soccer League; moved from USD's stadium to Snapdragon Stadium when it opened. Wave FC's first game in the new stadium set a since-surpassed league attendance record.

voyage.name: San Diego Legion
voyage.content: Plays in Major League Rugby, the top level of US rugby union.

voyage.name: Cygnet Theater
voyage.content: Live performances held regularly.

voyage.name: Fashion Valley
voyage.content: Nearly 200 stores and restaurants, including several department stores and a movie theater.

voyage.name: Westfield Mission Valley
voyage.content: Over 150 stores and restaurants, including a movie theater and the large Seau's sports restaurant.

voyage.name: Hazard Center
voyage.content: Much smaller than the big centers in the valley, but with a nice assortment of shops nevertheless.

voyage.name: Cousin's Candy Shop
voyage.content: Taffy made on the premises.

voyage.name: Fiesta de Reyes
voyage.content: A group of shops and restaurants operated by Delaware North, which runs concessions in other National Parks. Strolling musicians and beautiful flowers greet guests and there are often special (free) activities for children.

voyage.name: Johnson House
voyage.content: Victorian hats, related books, and jewelry in a 1869 style house.

voyage.name: Lowery's Hot Glass
voyage.content: Hand blown glass art made on premises.

voyage.name: Racine and Laramie
voyage.content: Gorgeous reconstruction of San Diego's first tobacco store. Offers a variety of historically related gifts, gentlemen's accessories, marbles and harmonicas for children, historic photos, knives, and of course tobacco, pipes, and cigars.

voyage.name: Casa De Reyes
voyage.content: Mexican food with lovely courtyard, and wandering musicians.

voyage.name: Cosmopolitan Restaurant and Hotel
voyage.content: A beautiful dining establishment in a building built by Juan Bandini in 1829. Later, in the 1860s, a second story was added and it became the Cosmopolitan Hotel. You can eat in the garden amid flowers, trees, and fountains or inside the wonderful historic building.

voyage.name: Hungry's Kitchen & Tap
voyage.content: Soup and salad (very limited), sandwiches, yards and half yards of beer, live music on weekend nights.

voyage.name: Old Town Mexican Café
voyage.content: Huge portions.

voyage.name: In-N-Out Burger
voyage.content: One of the two locations most conveniently reached from downtown (the other is in National City to the south).

voyage.name: Oggi's
voyage.content: Part of a local pizza chain in San Diego, they have a very extensive menu and also brew their own beer as well, with a stocked bar. Also has plenty of TVs to watch sports as well.

voyage.name: McGregors
voyage.content: A grill and ale house, great place to watch sports at, has pool tables, darts and shuffleboard.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Hacienda Hotel Old Town
Homewood Suites by Hilton San Diego Hotel Circle/SeaWorld Area
Handlery Hotel
voyage.content: A warm, friendly welcome and some big, lush rooms. Also has a hotel mini-bus to take you to SeaWorld.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Airport - Old Town
Town and Country
voyage.content: Resort with swimming pools, restaurants, spa facilities, golf, and beautiful gardens.

voyage.name: Fort Rosecrans
voyage.content: A former World War II military outpost, situated on Point Loma to protect the Naval Base on Coronado from attack by sea. The fort contains bunkers, weapons emplacements and the Fort Rosecrans National Cemetery, which holds a number of monuments including the USS Bennington Monument. An exhibit in Cabrillo National Monument displays some of the history of Fort Rosecrans.

voyage.name: MCRD San Diego
voyage.address: Public Entrance at Gate 5 at Washington Ave & Pacific Hwy
voyage.content: It is a military base located north of the airport, about 3 mi north of downtown San Diego and 2.5 mi around the runways from the airport terminals. Recruits from west of the Mississippi River are trained here while others from east of the Mississippi River are trained in Parris Island. Recruits graduate every Friday, and there is a Family Day, when the recruits' families can spend time with them on Thursday. This is

voyage.name: MCRD Museum Foundation
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 8:30AM-4PM; Foundation office closes at 3PM on Fridays and closed on weekends.
voyage.content: Museum exhibits the history of this installation and the history of the Marine Corps. They are open to the public outside of the Thursday and Friday graduation visits. They also have current and past yearbooks of San Diego graduates only. You must have the platoon number, month and year of graduation to be able to order yearbooks which may or may not be available. They do not have individual portraits available.

voyage.name: Cabrillo National Monument
voyage.price: $20/vehicle, $15/motorcycle, $10/person walking or bicycling in; national parks passes applicable
voyage.address: at the end of Catalina Boulevard
voyage.content: Located at the tip of Point Loma, Cabrillo National Monument commemorates Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo, who led the first European exploration to what is now the west coast of the United States, in 1542. Point Loma was one of the places where he stopped, and the first contact Europeans made with what would one day be California. The monument has a statue of Cabrillo and exhibits on his expedition in the visitor center.

voyage.name: Ocean Beach
voyage.address: Main lifeguard station at 1950 Abbott St
voyage.content: A large sandy beach, which cater to just about every beach-going type, offering designated surfing and swimming zones, which are monitored by the local life guards.

voyage.name: Dog Beach
voyage.content: At the northern end of Ocean Beach, dog lovers can bring their pets along for a romp in the waves or a swim in the flood channel.

voyage.name: Ocean Beach Municipal Pier
voyage.address: at the south end of the beach
voyage.content: Extends out over the waves and offers great views of the beautiful Pacific Ocean and coast. A tackle shop in the middle of the pier provides bait and supplies for the many fishing enthusiasts who frequent the area. This is one of the few places that visitors can fish without a California fishing license. Pole rentals are available at the bait shop as well.

voyage.name: Sunset Cliffs
voyage.address: along Sunset Cliffs Boulevard south of Ocean Beach
voyage.content: A lovely setting, Sunset Cliffs is an excellent place for sightseeing, picnics, watching sunsets (as the name suggests) or just driving along the rim of the beautiful cliffs along Sunset Cliffs Blvd. There is also a rather secluded beach there, but it's swim at your own risk. It is quite popular with the more adventurous and seasoned surfer as the surf is rather rough for the area. Be warned, however, that there are

voyage.name: Humphreys Concerts By the Bay
voyage.content: A concert series held every May through October, showcasing some famous entertainers (Crosby, Stills & Nash, Jewel, The Moody Blues, Bonnie Raitt) at Humphrey's Half Moon Inn & Suites. A wide variety of styles, from rock and jazz to comedy, blues and international music. Humphreys Restaurant also has live blues/jazz/disco/classic rock music every night in its lounge.

voyage.name: Shelter Island Boat Launching Ramp
voyage.content: Provides the closest access to the Pacific Ocean (approximately 3 miles away) of the four boat launch ramps on San Diego Bay. Restrooms and a large parking lot are immediately available. For visiting fishermen, the bait receivers, where anchovies and sardines can be purchased, are on the right side of the channel as you exit the harbor. The bait barges are open 24 hours per day.

voyage.name: Downwind Marine
voyage.content: Boating materials, supplies, and equipment are available here.

voyage.name: Karen’s Consignment Gallery
voyage.content: The place to go for silver, crystal, china, oriental rugs and lamps, and has been highly rated since opening day.

voyage.name: Seabreeze Nautical Books
voyage.content: A lot of boating products here, like navigational charts, sailing guides, plotting tools, and nautical-themed books and gifts.

voyage.name: Newport Avenue Antiques
voyage.content: Well known amongst antique collectors for the range of antique lighting and cigar and smoking accessories.

voyage.name: Hodads Restaurant
voyage.content: This restaurant is very popular, especially on weekends; sometimes the line outside reaches the street corner; their logo is a caricatured surfing burger with a caricature Hispanic person riding on top. they also have a Hodads van parked outside. It's a burger joint with fries and shirts and shoes are not required. A pair of seats inside is shaped like a car, and you sit in the driver seats. Their milkshakes are huge

voyage.name: Old Townhouse Restaurant
voyage.content: Family owned and operated for over 35 years; a local favorite for breakfast. They will also serve you bottomless cups of coffee.

voyage.name: Blue Water Seafood Ocean Beach
voyage.content: Oceanfront seafood restaurant with relaxing patio.

voyage.name: Kaiserhof
voyage.content: German food isn't the first thing most people associate with San Diego, but this place has been serving top quality Bavarian fare since 1980. Has a lively Biergarten with typical German pub food and a more sedate restaurant with a more extensive menu.

voyage.name: Long Story Irish Pub
voyage.content: Irish gastro pub with excellent food and a unique beer selection. .

voyage.name: Winstons
voyage.content: Nightly bands and dancing, karaoke and Monday night football. Watch the lines on the weekend as this place is packed with live bands, even during the daytime on summer Sundays.

voyage.name: Humphrey's Half Moon Inn
voyage.content: Located on Shelter Island, this resort offers many activities including live concerts.

voyage.name: MCRD Billeting (on base lodging)
voyage.content: On base lodging for active duty military, DoD and civilian personnel on TAD orders, retired military, and families of graduating new Marines from Wednesday-Saturday of graduation weeks only.

voyage.name: SeaWorld San Diego
voyage.price: $89 adults, $83 children ages 3-9, free for children under age 3 (parking $16 for cars, $21 for RVs and campers, and $11 for motorcycles)
voyage.content: Hours vary by season and day of week; typically 10AM-5PM in winter, 9AM-11PM in summer. A massive (200 acres) marine animal theme park with rides, lots of sea animals (dolphins, sea otters, arctic creatures, sharks, penguins, rays, manatees, etc.) and of course, shows of killer whales like Shamu.

voyage.name: Belmont Park
voyage.price: General admission free, ride tickets $1 each (rides take anywhere from 3-6 tickets each); unlimited ride passes available
voyage.hours: Open April–December, hours vary by season and day of week; typically 11AM-8PM
voyage.content: A seaside amusement park located near the southern end of Mission Beach, Belmont Park is a landmark with a number of shops, restaurants, an arcade, and a bunch of rides. The big attraction is the Giant Dipper, a historic roller coaster that is one of the only two remaining oceanfront roller coasters still operating on the west coast. Also popular is The Plunge, a historic indoor heated swimming pool that continues to

voyage.name: Mission Bay Aquatic Center
voyage.content: The aquatic center rents catamarans and other watercraft, as do several other franchises around the bay. Instructional lessons are available. The western half of the bay is "sail only" (powerboats 5 mph no wake) during the daytime.

voyage.name: Mission Bay Park
voyage.content: Encompassing the entirety of Mission Bay, offering opportunities for sailing, boating, swimming, jet ski, and other water sports. You can also take advantage of the park space surrounding the bay for walking, bicycling, picnicking, etc. There are many miles of hiking, biking, and running trails that have a moderate level of difficulty for runners and an easy level of difficulty for bicyclists. There are marvelous vie

voyage.name: Mission Bay Playground
voyage.address: East Mission Bay Drive on Mission Bay, south of Clairemont Drive
voyage.content: There are many playgrounds in the city, but this one is easily one of the best. For starters, it's a huge playground, with several elaborate play structures (one is built to resemble a pirate ship) and lots of elements for kids to explore. It's on the edge of Mission Bay and surrounded by expansive lawns perfect for kite-flying and playing sports.

voyage.name: Fiesta Island
voyage.content: This island in the middle of Mission Bay hosts the Fiesta Island Time Trial Series, hosted by the San Diego Bicycle Club. Competitors meet up to see who can ride the quickest 20k or improve the most. Single riders, tandems and teams are all welcome, and the event also hosts triathletes and world class road race athletes. There is always a waiting list for these trials, so early registration is vital if you want to ta

voyage.name: Mission Beach
voyage.content: This beach is one of the calmest, easiest places to ocean swim in San Diego area. You can also go scuba diving (off the shore are several dive wrecks). Or you can bicycle or rollerblade along the boardwalk (several stores nearby rent equipment).

voyage.name: Tourmaline Surfing Park
voyage.address: at the foot of Tourmaline Street in North Pacific Beach
voyage.content: A popular surfing spot for locals.

voyage.name: Pangea Outpost
voyage.content: Boutique and gift shop filled with shirts, books, home decorations, and art. The store is organized into small sections that have their own theme and specialties featuring local San Diego artists.

voyage.name: Bare Back Grill
voyage.content: Enjoy burgers made with organic New Zealand beef.

voyage.name: The Broken Yolk Café
voyage.content: As you can guess, the Broken Yoke specializes in eggs and omelettes but they also serve the regular breakfast fare of pancakes and French toast. It’s great for sitting down and recapping the previous night’s events. If you’re hungry enough, you can try their 12-egg omelette, loaded with all sorts of goodies to make it hard to finish. If you do, it’ll only cost you $2 and your name will be forever engraved on the wall

voyage.name: The Fishery
voyage.content: The retailer Pacific Shellfish Seafood Company was founded in 1979 but their attached restaurant debuted in 1998. With many different species of seasonal fresh fish in their cooler, you’ll be able to find something to tickle your taste buds from a simple tuna melt to a wild-caught Alaskan salmon. Since it’s a market too, you can verify that all the fish are fresh. And just in case you didn’t know what your particular

voyage.name: The French Gourmet
voyage.content: Has been serving delicious pastries and desserts to San Diego since 1979. You can stop in and try one of their many desserts or you can sit down for a whole meal. Their main entrées are just as tantalizing as the desserts. The breakfast menu includes omelettes, crepes and French toast and is served on weekends from 8AM-2:45PM and on weekdays 10AM-2:45PM. Lunch is served until 3PM and dinner is served everyday except

voyage.name: Kono’s
voyage.content: This eatery has the best budget breakfast in town, across from the entrance to Crystal Pier. A sign on the wall boasts how many days have passed since they last raised their prices; a figure which is easily over 365. On weekends the line outside gets so long you’d think it was nightclub, but the food is well worth the wait. They specialize in big breakfasts and breakfast burritos.

voyage.name: Mr. Frostie
voyage.content: A Pacific Beach institution, Mr. Frostie's has been selling soft serve ice cream since 1949. The simple, no frills menu also includes sandwiches and hot dogs, but it's the dipped ice cream cones, milkshakes, sundaes, and banana splits that will make this place outlast any trendy yogurt shop.

voyage.name: Rubio’s
voyage.content: Now a minor fast food restaurant chain in the western United States, but what’s significant about the one in PB is that it was the first. In 1983, founder Ralph Rubio capitalized on the unique flavor of Baja California taco stands by replicating one in San Diego (accommodating, of course, for local health codes). The beer-battered fish tacos, the carnitas and carne asada tacos were an immediate hit.

voyage.name: World Curry
voyage.content: Great variety of world curries and great happy hour beverage deals.

voyage.name: Oscar's Mexican Seafood
voyage.content: Small, local Mexican seafood chain specializing in ceviche, tacos, and tortas. Vegetarian options available.

voyage.name: Crushed
voyage.content: Brunch and dinner place known for their eggs benedicts and mimosas. Long wait time during the weekends.

voyage.name: Rocky's Crown Pub
voyage.content: Small, local pub serving 1/3 and 1/2 pound burgers. Cash only.

voyage.name: Sushi Ota
voyage.content: Though a bit far from the beach (but not from the bay), this small Japanese restaurant offers teriyaki, tempura, and sushi combos. Lunch specials are available. Best to call ahead and ask for reservations. Limited parking available in parking lot.

voyage.name: Olive Cafe
voyage.content: Nested between the bay and the beach, Olive Cafe provides breakfast scrambles, burritos, pancakes, breakfast bowls, and baked goods. Sister establishment for Olive Baking Company, which is a small, quick casual bakery, less than a block away. Parking is tough around the area and can get busy in the weekends.

voyage.name: Flamingo Deck
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu noon-midnight, Fri Sat noon-2AM, Sun 10AM-midnight
voyage.content: American beachside restaurant specializing in brunch, cocktails, and more. Capable for private events and occasional live music. Happy Hour M-F 3-6PM. Brunch Sa Su 10AM-2PM.

voyage.name: Baja Beach Cafe
voyage.content: Mexican restaurant on the boardwalk with a Mexican seafood specialty. Including fish tacos, hamburgers, margaritas, and more.

voyage.name: Lahaina Beach House
voyage.content: Cash only beach bar and grill along the boardwalk. Very popular with young people on the weekends, loud music and public restrooms here right by the beach.

voyage.name: Cass Street Bar and Grill
voyage.content: This comfortable, laid-back bar with deep sea fishing themed decor has a good crowd at practically any time of the day, night or week. It's a beer and wine bar, so cocktails drinks use a weak Asian vodka called Han Vodka, but the twelve or so beers on tap and various other bottled beers are enough to keep most customers happy. The profusion of TV screens make it a popular daytime sports bar, the pool tables and shuff

voyage.name: Lahaina Beach House
voyage.content: Laid-back bar with a deck facing the beach and boardwalk in a bungalow-type house. Good selection of national and local beers. Both breakfast and lunch/dinner is served on most days.

voyage.name: Moonshine Beach
voyage.content: Sister location of Moonshine Flats in downtown, the Pacific Beach location offers the same activities but in a larger space - including open air sections. The club offers line dancing lessons (select days), live country bands, karaoke, and club music. On Fridays and Saturdays, there is a cover charge can be avoided by signing up for the free guest list on their website.

voyage.name: Mavericks Beach Club
voyage.content: Two-story bar and restaurant with lots of TVs and an open-air area. Open for brunch on weekends with family-friendly menu. Converts to a popular club at night.

voyage.name: Backyard Kitchen and Tap
voyage.content: Lunch, dinner, and brunch on weekends, complete with seasonal cocktails with events on weekday nights. On Fridays and Saturdays, it converts to another popular nightclub.

voyage.name: Blue Palm
voyage.content: Coffee shop right by Mariners Basin. Also serves breakfast foods, tucked away.

voyage.name: Silver Spigot Cocktail Lounge
voyage.content: Mission Beach's premier longstanding dive bar. Loads of stuff on the walls, TVs with Chargers games, and pool. Reasonably priced drinks with locals inside. Quiet place to duck in and have a few jars off the beaten path.

voyage.name: ITH Beach Bungalow Surf Hostel
voyage.content: A small chain of tropical-themed hostels.

voyage.name: Beach Hut Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: Offering free on-site reserved parking, free Wi-Fi, landscaped pool/patio, queen beds, flat screened TV/cable, faux fireplaces.

voyage.name: Mission Bay Inn San Diego
voyage.content: A kid-friendly hotel off I-5 nearby.

voyage.name: Crystal Pier Hotel
voyage.content: The closest that you can get to staying on the beach. Built on the historic pier, these rooms offer amazing views and soothing ocean sounds to put you to sleep at night. With a room, you can actually drive out on the pier and park in front of your quarters.

voyage.name: Pacific View Inn
voyage.content: Rooms are reasonably priced and include kitchenettes.

voyage.name: Surfer Beach Hotel
voyage.content: Right on the Pacific Ocean and features a retro boutique-style décor, a popular onsite restaurant, and private guestroom balconies.

voyage.name: Catamaran Resort Hotel
voyage.content: Large, Polynesian-themed 4-star hotel right between the beach and Mission Bay. The high rise kid-friendly hotel offers, pools, hot tubs, restaurants, bonfires, and parrot encounters.

voyage.name: San Diego Mission Bay Resort
voyage.content: Resort on the eastern end of Mission Bay. Loads of family friendly activities right off the 5 freeway.

voyage.name: Athenaeum Music & Arts Library
voyage.hours: Tue Thu-Sat 10AM-5:30PM, Wed 10AM-8:30PM, closed Sundays and Mondays
voyage.content: A nonprofit, membership library which sponsors art exhibitions, concerts, lectures, and art classes.

voyage.name: Birch Aquarium at Scripps
voyage.price: $17 adults, $14 teens, $13 seniors, $12.50 children, $12 students, free for children age 2 and under
voyage.content: The public center for the renowned Scripps Institution of Oceanography (of University of California, San Diego), this aquarium has many fantastic exhibits, with oceanic species from all over the Pacific Ocean displayed, as well as sharks, a tide pool, a large kelp tank, and a coral reef (with actual living coral). The museum also has some spectacular views of the ocean and La Jolla as well as some nifty tide pools wh

voyage.name: The Cave Store
voyage.content: Built on top of a sea cave, this gift shop offers tours of a small cavern open to the ocean.

voyage.name: Children's Pool Beach
voyage.content: This beach is a favorite breeding spot for harbor seals. The beach is closed Dec 15-May 15 during breeding season, but you can still observe the seals from a safe distance. This beach used to be the children's beach, and there is an ongoing dispute between animal rights supporters and others who disagree about who should own the beach. Depending on the current turn of events, swimming may or may not be permitted. Occ

voyage.name: Mount Soledad
voyage.content: A prominent landmark just to the east of La Jolla, overlooking much of San Diego. The top of the mountain is adorned by the Mount Soledad Easter Cross and Veterans Memorial. It is home to many rabbits and couples. Sunrise and sunset are the two favorite times to go here. The twisty roads leading to the hill are full of plant life and give access to multimillion dollar hobbit homes which look much smaller from the str

voyage.name: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego La Jolla
voyage.price: $10 adults, $5 students/seniors, military/age 25 and under free
voyage.content: Permanent and changing contemporary art exhibits.

voyage.name: Salk Institute of Biological Studies
voyage.content: Near UCSD is this architectural monolith; the structure for this noted institution is built out of unfinished concrete and perched atop the cliffs overlooking the ocean. It is one of famed modernist Louis Kahn's most important works. Two symmetrical buildings stare at each other across a courtyard, the length of which runs a wide river which reverses into a pool and, through a small waterfall, down towards the dining

voyage.name: University of California, San Diego
voyage.content: A combination of a small liberal arts college and a large research university, UCSD has a good reputation locally and offers some interesting sights. You can take a walk around the campus and observe a number of famous artworks and architectural structures.

voyage.name: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve
voyage.price: If you walk into the park, it’s free. Otherwise, parking fees are $10 (winter) or $12 (summer) per car M-Th, and $12 (winter) or $15 (summer) per car F-Su and holidays
voyage.hours: Gates open at 7:15AM and close at sunset. Visitor center 9AM-6PM summer, 10AM-4PM fall-spring. Interpretive nature walks leave the visitor center at 10AM and 2PM on weekends and holidays.
voyage.content: No bikes, dogs, food and beverages allowed.

voyage.name: Torrey Pines Gliderport
voyage.content: Learn to hang glide.

voyage.name: La Jolla Cove
voyage.content: A very popular beach for swimming, scuba diving and snorkeling, set against beautiful sea cliffs. In 2026, it was ranked by TripAdvisor as no. 1 in the United States and no. 7 in the world. The bluffs above the beach are grassy, making a great spot for picnics. Keep in mind that La Jolla Cove is part of the San Diego-La Jolla Underwater Park Ecological Reserve, so fishing, scavenging, or "swimming devices" (surfboard

voyage.name: Windansea Beach
voyage.content: This beach has no facilities, but is notable for playing host to a great number of talented and famous surfers. The simple "Surf Shack" structure there has been designated a historic landmark. There are huge, smoothly sculpted rocks on this beach that are fun to climb on and look at.

voyage.name: Marine Street Beach
voyage.content: A local beach with some rough and dangerous surf. This is a great spot for body surfing and body boarding. No facilities are available here.

voyage.name: La Jolla Shores
voyage.content: In north La Jolla, this beach has some of the gentlest waves of any beach in San Diego. The beach is notable for being near the Scripps Institution of Oceanography campus and it contains the Scripps Pier. This is one of the only beach boat launching areas in La Jolla, so it's a popular spot for kayaking and surfing.

voyage.name: Black's Beach
voyage.address: in north La Jolla just below Torrey Pines State Park
voyage.content: Set against high cliffs, Black's Beach is the largest nude beach in the country. There are two parts of the beach. There is the southern part in the City of San Diego, where nudity is not allowed (although this rule is rarely enforced), and the northern part in Torrey Pines State Park, where clothing is purely optional. Black's Beach has one of the most powerful beach breaks in Southern California, making it a popula

voyage.name: Torrey Pines State Beach
voyage.content: Stretched along Torrey Pines State Park and set against gorgeous cliffs, this beach is one of the most beautiful around. A salt marsh at the north end of the beach empties into the ocean. The beach is also a popular one for surfing and body boarding.

voyage.name: Torrey Pines Golf Course
voyage.content: A stunning seaside public golf course noted for hosting the PGA Tour Farmers Insurance Open every January or February.

voyage.name: La Jolla Country Club
voyage.content: Private members-only club. Strict attire, cell phone, and tipping guidelines.

voyage.name: Westfield UTC
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 10AM-9PM, Sat 10AM-8PM, Sun 11AM-7PM (individual store hours vary)
voyage.content: An outdoor shopping mall just outside of La Jolla, in the University City area. Basically anything you'd find in your average suburban shopping mall with the addition of an ice skating rink, called Ice Town.

voyage.name: Warwick's Books
voyage.content: Independent bookstore with books, gifts, stationary, and author events.

voyage.name: Brockton Villa
voyage.content: Well known for their breakfast and lunch menus.

voyage.name: Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar
voyage.address: 8970 University Center Ln, adjacent to the Hyatt Regency La Jolla at Aventine
voyage.content: For when you are feeling laissez-faire with the credit card and want some filet mignon or ribeye.

voyage.name: Marketplace Grille
voyage.content: Lebanese grill with kebabs and salmon bowls, etc.

voyage.name: Shores Restaurant
voyage.address: 8110 Camino del Oro, in the La Jolla Shores Hotel
voyage.content: Offering seasonal cuisine, oceanfront views and a great selection of wines. Delicious American comfort food.

voyage.name: Caroline's Seaside Cafe
voyage.content: Casual cafe situated right next to the beach on the UCSD-SIO campus. The cafe serves breakfast items including eggs, pancakes and lunch items including sandwiches and burgers. Seated is first-come-first-served casual setting (so no waiters only servers). Parking is limited and may need a UCSD parking pass on weekdays, however, 2-hr street parking is available.

voyage.name: Don Carlos Taco Shop
voyage.content: Small Tex-Mex/Mexican taco shop that also serves burritos, tortas, quesadillas, and enchiladas. Specializes in variants of California burritos including vegetarian ones. Limited parking nearby.

voyage.name: The Taco Stand
voyage.content: La Jolla location of the medium-sized chain of taco shops featuring hand-made tortillas. Also serves burritos and churros and also has vegetarian options. The location typically has long lines, but online ordering and pickup is available.

voyage.name: The Marine Room
voyage.content: Fine dining establishment right by the water, it also serves as an event venue for private events and more. Connected to the La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club, Inc. Since 1941.

voyage.name: Raymundo's Taco Shop
voyage.content: Mexican restaurant. Reasonable food with loads of staple options. No public restroom.

voyage.name: Verdes El Ranchero
voyage.content: Locally owned longstanding Mexican restaurant. Great decor and good food inside. Margaritas are good and the food is reasonably priced for the area.

voyage.name: Gata
voyage.content: Wine and tapas bar in downtown. Serves a big selection of wines, with a good atmosphere.

voyage.name: Orli La Jolla
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with kombucha and comfortable rooms and suites.

voyage.name: Embassy Suites San Diego-La Jolla
voyage.content: All-suites hotel.

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency La Jolla at Aventine
voyage.content: Sitting on 11 acres, 419 remodeled rooms, spacious VIP suites, wireless high-speed Internet, and 32,000 square feet of flexible function space.

voyage.name: Estancia La Jolla Hotel & Spa
voyage.content: A rancho style conference and vacation resort located adjacent to the University of California at San Diego.

voyage.name: Grande Colonial Hotel
voyage.content: A landmark, historic hotel overlooks the shores of the Pacific Ocean and ideally located just steps away from the beach.

voyage.name: Hilton La Jolla Torrey Pines
voyage.content: Bluff-top Hilton hotel overlooking the famous Torrey Pines golf course.

voyage.name: La Valencia
voyage.content: Historic Spanish-style luxury hotel built in 1926, famed for its views of the La Jolla Cove and its Sunday brunch.

voyage.name: The Lodge at Torrey Pines
voyage.content: Rustic alpine-style hotel adjacent to the PGA Championship Torrey Pines Golf Course. This is a high-end resort and spa. The A. R. Valentien restaurant, named for the California artist, overlooks the 18th hole of the Torrey Pines golf course. Works by Valentien are on exhibit throughout the dining room.

voyage.name: Residence Inn La Jolla
voyage.content: A very pleasant suite-style hotel. It is in a quiet area of La Jolla, very close to the University of California at San Diego. The rooms are spacious, with full kitchens. It includes a pool and hot tubs located close to the rooms. There are BBQ grills in the small common patio between the buildings. Within walking distance there is a nice shopping center with several restaurants and grocery stores. Free high speed in

voyage.name: Chicano Park
voyage.content: A park distinctive for being the site of a militant takeover like Berkeley Park in Berkeley CA, by individuals affiliated with the Chicano Movement resisting assimilation in the likes of Cesar Chavez, with the main attraction being extensive murals beneath the Coronado Bridge superstructure. There is also the Chicano Park Museum and Cultural Center on site and a statue of General Zapata.

voyage.name: San Diego State University Aztecs
voyage.content: College basketball enthusiasts may be familiar with "The Show", SDSU's famously rowdy student section. They play their home games at Viejas Arena (formerly Cox Arena) on the SDSU campus. The Aztecs college baseball team plays at Tony Gwynn Stadium (also on the SDSU campus). The college football team opened the new Snapdragon Stadium in Mission Valley, built on part of the site of the team's former home of San Diego S

voyage.name: The Adams Avenue Street Fair
voyage.price: Entrance is free, but the food and beer gardens can be a bit pricey
voyage.content: Held over the last weekend in late September, showcases local business and organizations, various food and tchotchke vendors, and six stages of live music across the three blocks of this main drag in Normal Heights.

voyage.name: Kensington
voyage.content: Centered along Adams Avenue east of CA-15, is a small community with much charm. Instead of going here for excitement, you should go to relax. Take some time to walk around the neighborhood and see all of the old houses and their well kept gardens. Get a cup of coffee at Kensington Cafe and then enjoy it at the park that surrounds the local library. Around dinner take the time to eat at the local restaurants and then

voyage.name: Folk Arts Rare Records
voyage.content: Established in 1967, Folk Arts Rare Records specializes in folk and country, but has a great variety of styles and genres in stock (from Surf to Pop, Blues to Metal, Zydeco to Rock).

voyage.name: Replay Toys Boutique
voyage.content: Huge range of new, used, and vintage toys.

voyage.name: Verbatim Books
voyage.price: On the expensive side for a used bookstore - many books are $6-20; more for rare or high-end books
voyage.hours: Sun Mon Wed Thu 10AM-6PM, Tue 12-6PM, Fri Sat 10AM-7PM
voyage.content: Beautiful used bookstore with a great selection. Highlights include many vintage series and magazines, ornamental books, political zines, a large collection of classic children's chapter books and YA novels, and a large and eclectic foreign-language section.

voyage.name: The Book Catapult
voyage.content: Small but very well curated bookstore.

voyage.name: The Big Kitchen
voyage.content: This restaurant is so named because the kitchen is bigger than the rest of the restaurant. "Judy The Beauty (on Duty)" is usually there serving up great food (mainly breakfast, but also lunch), with a cheerful attitude. Take time to appreciate the bumper stickers and celebrity posters on the walls - Whoopi Goldberg once worked here.

voyage.name: Bleu Boheme
voyage.content: Charming, rustic neighborhood French brasserie in the heart of Kensington. They feature a prix fixe Bohemian menu every night from 5-6PM, all night on Tuesdays. Try the moules frites in Roquefort sauce.

voyage.name: Ponces Mexican Restaurant
voyage.content: Ponces has been renovated, offering a bar and better seating but it still offers some of the best American Mexican food in San Diego. Not authentic Mexican food, but good American Mexican food. Get there with enough time to wait and if you don't want dine in call for take out.

voyage.name: Red Fox Steakhouse and Piano Bar
voyage.content: Charming place where it's easy to imagine you've time-traveled to the early 1970s. Don't expect cutting-edge cuisine, but when your parents or grandparents wanted to have a nice evening out, they probably went somewhere like this. The bar furnishings came from a 17th-century English pub - think mood lighting and lots of dark leather and oak. Also a good place for a cocktail or two. Live music nightly.

voyage.name: Zia Gourmet Pizza
voyage.content: Zias is home to some of the most unique and tastiest pizzas in all San Diego. You can order by the slice or a whole pie. The types of pizza range from the traditional cheese (three types) to the most famous, eggplant (cranberries, walnuts, yogurt, and eggplant). All food served is kosher and halal and there are vegan options as well. The owner and head chef constantly walks around and asks how everything tastes.

voyage.name: Pomegranate
voyage.content: Russian and Georgian (the country, not the US state) food. Highlights include adjaruli (a bread boat filled with cheese and egg), borscht, and excellent cabbage rolls.

voyage.name: North Park Creamery
voyage.content: Soft-serve ice cream, with the option of a "dip" that forms a hardened shell around the ice cream. Good vegan and dairy-free options.

voyage.name: Nomad Donuts
voyage.content: Donuts and bagels. Good vegan options.

voyage.name: Ranchos Cocina
voyage.content: Mexican restaurant with extensive vegan options.

voyage.name: Blind Lady Ale House
voyage.content: With a pub vibe and aesthetic, BLAH's a fantastic place to drink a wide selection of local craft brew and munch on some pizza. During the week it's not nearly as crowded--you'll be able to find a spot on the long wooden tables. If you ride your bike there, you can get a 10% discount when you show your helmet at the bar.

voyage.name: Club Kensington
voyage.content: A quaint hipster bar that offers music on the weekends.

voyage.name: Kensington Cafe
voyage.content: This coffee shop, loved by the locals, serves coffee, tea, food and even spumoni.

voyage.name: Lestat's Coffee House
voyage.content: Lestat's never closes, ever. Aside from the specialty coffee drinks and the local pastries, the walls are covered with art for sale, and the next door stage has nightly shows and open mics. Free wifi attracts all sorts of local characters and the back is always packed with people. They have a sister location in University Heights along Park Avenue.

voyage.name: Living Room Coffeehouse
voyage.content: A regular neighborhood coffee spot that's a popular study space for many college students given its proximity to SDSU.

voyage.name: Lafayette Hotel
voyage.content: Historic hotel that was at one time a preferred San Diego destination for Hollywood's elite. The Olympic-sized pool was designed by Johnny Weismuller of Tarzan fame. On summer weekends they host often fairly raucous pool parties.

voyage.name: Casa Miranda
voyage.content: A small mom-and-pop nightly rental apartment complex. Well furnished, on a residential street.

voyage.name: San Diego Zoo Safari Park
voyage.alt: formerly the San Diego Wild Animal Park
voyage.price: $58 adults, $48 children, free for children under 3 (Parking is $15/vehicle, $20/RV)
voyage.content: Sister park to the San Diego Zoo in Balboa Park, the Safari Park is a massive (1,800 acres) zoo with large, naturalistic free-range enclosures containing animals from all over the world. Highlights include the huge Africa area, the California Condor exhibit, and a tram ride which takes you past some of the large free-range areas (extra admission required).

voyage.name: San Pasqual Battlefield State Historic Park
voyage.content: On December 6, 1846, one of the bloodiest battles of the Mexican-American war took place here. The visitor center on-site has displays on the history of the site.

voyage.name: Bernardo Winery
voyage.content: A winery that dates back to 1889 on what was a Spanish land grant.

voyage.name: Los Peñasquitos Canyon Preserve
voyage.content: A large park stretching several miles between the I-5/I-805 intersection and I-15, just south and roughly parallel to SR-56. There is very beautiful scenery which can be explored via the system of hiking, biking and equestrian trails. The park also contains a few historical landmarks, including the Rancho de los Penasquitos, one of the oldest surviving homes in the region, dating back to 1823. Tours of the house are

voyage.name: Marian Bear Memorial Park
voyage.content: It's in the San Clemente Canyon along SR-52 from I-5 to I-805. This large park contains some very scenic trails.

voyage.name: Mission Trails Regional Park
voyage.address: Visitor Center, One Father Junipero Serra Trail
voyage.content: This massive park along the San Diego River between San Diego and Santee is a hidden jewel among the city's park system. Consisting mostly of rugged, hilly scrubland, Mission Trails offers an excellent diversion from the hustle and bustle of the city. Numerous trails criss cross through the park, and there's an excellent visitor center with exhibits on the flora, fauna, and the human history in the area. You can also

voyage.name: Tecolote Canyon Natural Park
voyage.content: Tecolote Canyon is a narrow coastal valley in the neighborhood of Clairemont which offers miles of trails open to hiking and biking. The visitor center at the mouth of the canyon offers exhibits on the flora and fauna found in the park.

voyage.name: Vertical Hold
voyage.content: The largest full service indoor climbing gym in the San Diego area.

voyage.name: 99 Ranch Market
voyage.content: A mostly California chain of Asian supermarkets. Here you can come face to face with your dinner - live! The entire back wall of this full-size supermarket is the fish department - and many of them are still swimming. This is such a special and unique market that a local cooking school offers group tours.

voyage.name: Karl Strauss Brewery Gardens
voyage.content: Hidden behind the trees in the San Diego Tech Center, Karl Strauss Brewery Gardens feels more like a high-end sushi place than a brewery/restaurant complete with a koi pond. Lots of outdoor seating. Gets very crowded during the week for lunch & dinner. They serve their own beers on tap and have an extensive menu.

voyage.name: HIVE
voyage.content: Korean food and a great place for karaoke.

voyage.name: K Sandwiches
voyage.content: A local favorite, with incredibly good, cheap, and authentic banh mi (Vietnamese sandwiches).

voyage.name: O'Brien's
voyage.content: This place has a great low-key friendly atmosphere. There is outdoor seating and a wonderful selection of Belgian local microbrews, with an extra emphasis on hoppy brews. They have a surprisingly good bar food as well.

voyage.name: Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Sorrento Mesa/La Jolla
voyage.content: New state-of-the-art hotel with fresh, healthy food options and Starbucks coffee. Complimentary WiFi.

voyage.name: Four Points by Sheraton San Diego
Hampton Inn and Suites San Diego - Poway
voyage.content: Free hot breakfast and internet.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn San Diego Del Mar
Homewood Suites San Diego Del Mar
voyage.content: Don't be fooled by the name. This hotel is not in Del Mar, but in the neighborhood of Sorrento Valley. The location is more convenient to points south of the I-5/I-805 merge.

voyage.name: Rancho Valencia Resort
voyage.content: Luxury resort, featuring a spa, tennis and golf, with 49 suites.
